fileDesc.titleStmt: DIARIES AND LETTERS OF PHILIP HENRY, M.A., OF BROAD OAK, FLINTSHIRE, A.D. 1631-1696. ED. BY MATTHEW HENRY LEE. LONDON: KEGAN PAUL, TRENCH & CO. 1882.

text.p:
I bless God, I am safe and well at London. I came from Oxford yesterday morning alone, but the Lord was with me; it was a long journey but I was stirring betimes. I was nine miles on my way before eight o'clock, and came an hour or two before sun-set to Thistleworth. Towards the end of my journey, for three or four miles, where was most danger it pleased God I had Company, which was a great mercy. I met many soldiers upon the way, going homewards upon their disbanding, towards their several countries, and I was sometimes afraid
of them. They were by two & three in a company, but the Lord preserved me. This morning I came to Chelsea, where I saw my sisters, in health, blessed bee God, and overjoyed to see me; from thence, this afternoon, to London. I have been with cousin Thomas Hotchkis, from whom I received a letter to Sr Orlando Bridgman from Mr. Eddow; and, to-morrow, I purpose, God willing, to wait upon his Lordship, expecting a charge from him, in the first place, about conformity, wherein yet I shall do as I see cause, in case I should be continued at Worthenbury. The ministers here are generally unanimous, and resolved. Dr. Sheldon was installed Bishop of London to-day. The King is gone into the country for a fortnight during the trial of his father's Judges to prevent petitions. I sleep to- night at Mrs. Kingstons who desires to be remembered to you, and to Mr. Puleston, and his wife. I wrote to you, by the last post, from Oxford. Commend me to sister Mary, and all that ask of me. Dear heart, make much of thyself, and love me; and the Lord everlasting be thy Sun and Shield! So prays,

Your letter to me I recd & ire mother also her's, in the former an account of your being busy, at which we were glad, in the later of your being not well, & that troubles us, but wee are in hope, that this night's post will bring us better tidings, that it proves not an Ague, as you fear, but a sudden ache the effect of your being wet in the shower & not shifting more then your shoes when you came to Isle. however wee desire to acquiesce in the will of God in whose hand our times are, and at whose dispose are all our ways, who doth always that which is just & righteous, & always that which is best to those that love him. I am at the writing of this at Boreatton where I expected your mother this morning, as wee appointed, but instead of coming herself, she sends Roger with your two letters, & her desire to me to answer them from hence by the way of Shrewsb. they are all well, blessed bee God, both there & here, my Lord Paget intended to have gone from hence tomorrow, which hastened me hither a week sooner than I expected & cause a fayleur at home yesterday, on Chapel-day, but his stay now is till next week; I am comforted that you acknowledge God in your distemper, and are prepared to receive with patience what he appoints; The two last subjects wee were upon when you left Br. O., Faith & Repentance, I hope were made profitable to you; hee that truly Repents of sin and truly
believes in the Lord J. Xt nothing can come amiss to him, things present are his, things to come are his, Life, Death, this world and t'other world; Though you are at distance from us, you are near to him who according to his promise is a present help to those that fear him in every time of need; our poor prayers for you, you may bee sure are not, shall not bee wanting, that if the Lord please you may have health to ply the work you came about, that you may serve the will of God in your generation, if otherwise, that you may be satisfied, in what hee doth, and so wee by his grace shall endeavour to bee also. Commend us to Mr. Doolitol & his wife, whose tender love to you & care concerning you, wee shall always acknowledge with all thankfulness; also to Cozin Rob~t, who I know will help to bear your Burden; The Lord Almighty bless you, my dear child, and cause his face to shine upon you, and send us good news in your next concerning you. Amen. This from

The experience which I have had of your very great Candor, together with the particular leave you were pleased to give me of Applying myself to you, as there might bee occasion of this nature, are my encouragemt to trouble your Lordship with these few lines. I understand, there are several Protestant Dissenters of your Diocese, that being excommunicate, are in danger of being cast into Prison by writs remaining in the Sheriffs hands for that purpose; concerning whom, when I was with you at Chester, you were pleased to say, it was not for their mere non-conformity but for witholding their Church dues; having made Inquiry about it, I doo find that there are but few of them chargeable with that neglect, & of those few, there is one William David of Myvod on whose behalf the Minr of the Place hath written the enclosed, whereby it will appear, that his default therein was not wilful & usual but merely accidental, which when your Lordship sees, I hope, it will prevail to obtain from you his discharge. And for the rest, who suffer for not conforming, I have personal acquaintance with divers of them, both about
Wrexham in Montgom-shire, particularly with Mr. Walter Griffiths & Richard Gardiner, & Evan Roberts, and have reason to believe concerning them, that they are Religious, sober, peaceable men, though under Dissatisfactions in the things imposed, and being such, I would entreat your lordship on their behalf that your lenity may be extended towards them, and the rather considering, that the casting of them into the Jail is like to be the Ruin both of themselves and of their Families as to this world, which I am confident can be no way pleasing to you in the Reflection. Besides, the Procdgs ag~t them, if I bee not misinformed, are upon Presentmts made in your Predecessor's days long since, and if in other cases, the Action dyes with the Person it were but reasonable it should in this also. Would your Lordship please, to forbear but for a while highest Act of Severity toward them, it may be upon further conference w. them and knowledge of them you will find them other Persons then they are Represented to you to bee. I humbly beg your lordship's pardon for my Boldness with you herein and subscribe myself,
For the Right Reverend Wm lord Bishop of St Asaph.

note.value: 4. MR. HENRY'S FIRST LETTER TO HIS SON ON GOING TO GRAY'S INN.

text.p: For Mr. Matthew Henry to bee left with Mr. Darrack at the Golden Trumpet within Aldersgate. London. Son Matthew,

I received both your letters, the one on Friday, the other yesterday, rejoicing to understand thereby the great
goodness of God to you in your journey, & particularly that your Company proved no worse, than it seems it did, which wee were much afraid of. I hope you will now in the first place make a business of fixing somewhere, so as may best conduct to your great end in going, wherein wee beg direction for you from Heaven, which appoints the bounds of our Habitation; forget not the rules given you, consult health & wholesomness, convenience & honesty, your next I trust will tel us you are so fitted. The Omens you mention doe little affect me, supposing them all true, which I much question, but perhaps they doe others; I would be now glad of a fuller account of the Substantials, as far as they are yet or may bee known. Wee remain as yet, thanks bee to God, in the same circumstances of Mercy in which you left us, wishing you some of our sweet air, which is now more then at other times of the year perfumed, instead of your offensive town-smels, against which you have need to arm your self, especially at first till you are used to them.

My jealousy over you was the effect of my dear love to you and the account you give me of your company comforts me, for I apprehended & doe so still, that your Danger in London will lye much that way, thereof. still keep up your watch & bee strong in the grace of J. Xt. for when you trust to sf. you are gone. I like it well that you spent last Tuesday as you did, only supposing Dr. T.'s lecture to bee in the Aftern. I understand not where you dind; if with Dr. Humph. it was not well, for fasting & asp. going so into Assemblies may bee very prejudicial to your health ere you are aware, thereof. by no means use it not. I shall long to hear from your Aunt Ann, how you p~formed in that journey, & what she thinks as to her coming hither; might you not cast to come down together, either in Coach or on Horse-back, either from London (you coming back from Oxf. thither to have her company) or from Oxf. I sending a double Horse &
she coming by Coach thither, or how else you can contrive it between you, for the truth is, I much desire to see her.

Our good God, that orders all, orders it for good to them accord to his will. last night was buried in Whitch. Mr. Ralph Tushingham, who broke his neck by a fall from his Horse, no body with him, betw. Wrenb. mil & Bromhal Green, coming from an Ale house at Wrenb. where Mr. Star. Mr. Written & hee had drunk hard; there is talk that many are like to lose much by him; Mr. Corbt sends to me to write to you to hearken them out a minr. for Cockshute either at London or Oxf. you know their circumstances & what a one will please them. Wee did not go to Rhuabon on Witnessed. in regard of the discomposures that were in the Neighbourhood, which are now allayed, upon occas. of the D. of. Ms invasion & the proclaiming of him Traytr which the Post before brought tidings of; I keep home, hear little, & say less; It is our unhappiness, to bee suspected p.sons without cause & to be exposed accordingly, though quiet in the land, but God is righteous & wise & good, & knows how to bring glory to hims. & good to the remnant out of all events whatsoever, even out of the eater meat, & out ye strong sweetness, & out of the lion's carcase, honey. This night wee expect to see Cos. Th. Bowker & his new Bride. Have you not taken a turn at Whitehal yet, to see the nest in the Ortyard, whence your poor Father came? your uncles either of them or your Aunts, would accompany you. Commend us all to them; I write not, because by you they hear of us. Wee hear that Chester Fair is forbidden which is a disappointmt to many londoners & others. Your Mother gives you her Blessing, your Sisters their kind love. I suppose by this time, you are in the Hal again in commons, where you must bee careful to behave yours. with all soberness, for many eyes are upon you; you want your Supper-companion, your individuus comes there, to whom we desire to bee remembered, beseeching the lord to direct your way in everything & to keep you humble, & serious, & in his fear always, which is the daily prayer of

note.value: 8. TO PHILIP HENRY IN CHESTER CASTLE FROM M. H.

text.p:
We received yrs last night by Ann Huxley, and though it troubles us to think yt yrs are there (and it is the more grievous because you have used to bee so little abroad) yet the account you give of your circumstances, doth somewhat comfort us, wee can see the cup mix't, and cannot but acknowledge the goodness of yt God yt mixes it, and especially that puts honey upon ye Rod, hoping that as afflictions abound, consolations will abound. no Bars nor bolts nor guards can exclude him. I am very sorry I cannot come to see you, indeed many of my friends are against it and therefore I submit, hoping and praying & waiting for a comfortable meeting in God's due time, and yet am apt to think I could come without danger. My Mother is just now gone to Hanmer to ye Burial of old Aunt Mattocks, who died on Sat. night. Cousin Benyon called of her, and left her service to you. We are all well (blessed bee God) Sis. El's ague returns not. My Mother thinks to send Sister Sarah to see you, upon Thursday, if room will be had in the Chester Coach, if not, it must be deferred till there is, but she is overjoyed to think of seeing you. Wee think to send this week for my Sisters, and I think to go ye day before, and so bring ym home with me, if Mr. H. & my Lady would let ire daughtrs or (which p~haps would bee better at is time) some one of ym come hither, wee could send (for one) with my sisters, if wee have orders frm you by ye Bearer Owen Brown & should bee glad of it. Wee expect ye chimney-men here to-day, for yey are come into our Town, yey gave an account of yeir buisness to ye Justices yesterday, who for ought I understand could not or would not gainsay them, & so there's no remedy but patience. Adieu. Pears has paid for ye Bak-house chimney at Bron: They are now carrying ye last load out of ye little meadow. 5 Load in all. No more but affectionate love, duty, service from us all as due
wishing the eternal God may bee ire Refuge & underneath may bee ye Everlasting Arms I rest
I forgot to tel you yt I was yesterd. at Will. Cross, my Lady talks of going to see her friends in Bonds but when I know not, she offers to take my Mo. along with her in her Coach at any time.
You are enquired for by frnds & neighbrs with no small concernedness. The Chimney men are just now gone: and are paid 4sh for ye Kill-chimney, and much ado I had to save Tho. Matthews' Bake house.

note.value: 9. FROM PHILIP HENRY IN CHESTER CASTLE TO MRS. HENRY AT BROAD OKE.

text.p:
I continue very well, at present, thanks bee to God! and feel nothing yet of the Inconveniences of a prison; we are better accommodated, as I acquainted you in my last, then wee could have expected, though wee must pay for it. Just now six Minrs N. C. are brought in hither from lancashire, more than before, so far are wee from enlargmt, but our times are in God's hand, who hath sent us hither, I am confident, for good, though how or which way or wherein I know not, but hee is faithful that hath promised. My Chamber fellows & I differ someth. in our apprehensions of things past, which will not bee helped, but for the unseen th. that are to come that are Eternal, wee are all one. Our Afternoons, till late, are filled with visitants, who love us & wish us well & are kind to us, but wee cannot doe with them what wee would. Cos. Crew hath been an hour with me this morning she brought me a quart of Aqu. Mirab. which I would have had her take back again, till more need, but she would not. I have not yet opened yt little bottle I brought with me, since I came, not wanting it, & being more afraid of what might heat
me, in regard wee have no drink but strong (unless very seldom) neither morning, noon, nor night, which may turn to Feavorish distempers, wanting exercise - I have not trodden on the ground since Sat. which using mys. to in mornings I thought ye want of it might bee prejudicial, but hitherto it is not; I have not tasted Butter yet with bread since I came from home. This dinner wee had Beans and Bacon, Sammon &c. but I am careful with I eat, not Fishes & Fleshes. Mrs. Wenlock was to see me yesterday & brought me a bottle of wine. I bestow all of that kind in Common, my Companions strangers here. This Aftern. ye Citizens meet on Rood-dee with Halberds, they think to take the Oath. Mrs. Clive is here, Mr. Woodh. I hope recovers, & wn well comes in again. I have seen Mr. H. but it is at distance. Let me hear from you, how you doe & the children &c. as oft as you can. Show not my letters. When you think fit to send for them from Salop, Send love to Matth. Our Guards change every hour, which makes it so very hard to come to us, else wee might oblige them. I would gladly see him, but when or how I know not, I think there's little danger of any harm to him here, if there bee none at home, at his return. Love to Sarah & El'nor, & to Ann D. & to all ye rest of you, doe with you can to get to heaven your selves & to help one another thither. Prepare for further Sufferings, to which it may bee these th. are but the Preamble but all is well that ends everlastingly well. Thanks for all ire love & faithfulness to me, & Patience with me; the lord will reward it. One of my Fellow Prisoners last night received a letter from his wife subscribed - so I rest dear Husband in all Duty & Obedience your Obedient wife - Such is lancashire kindness, but deeds exceed words - I am in short most entirely & most affectionately thine.

note.value: 10. TO MATTHEW HENRY AT GRAY'S INN.

text.p:
Wee are glad to hear of Gods goodness to you in your journey, going out & coming in, & of the pleasing circumstances which hee hath brought you to in the place where you are, concerning which you doe well not to call it settlement, for our
present state here below is & must be a Tabernacle-state, wee are but strangers & pilgrims, as all our Fathers were, the world is our Inn, & the place wherein you are, bearing that name, it should mind you daily, what your condition is in it; you are to count upon being there but a while & to manage your self, your time, your Affections, your conversation accordingly; whilst you reckon, you have no continuing City here, you are the more concerned to make one sure that is to come. It pleases God to lengthen out his displeasure towards us in this neighbourhood in the continuance of the Small Pox which hath taken away many, or's are yet preserved, to his name bee the praise, in whose hand our times are & at whose dispose are all our ways.

Tho. Haunch. was here to-day, paying his Rent, honestly; the rest I hope, will bee had ere long, but the general complaint is, that nothing takes money, The price of Cattle & Corn is low, & pity it is that Plenty should bee a grievance; it is but a little while, I am sure, since the complaint was high & loud, the other way. God in mercy secure the Gospel to us, though he feed us with the Bread of Adversity & give us Tears to drink in other matters! The Dr gave them a good Sermon. Nov. 5. from 2 Cor. 1. 10. There was generally in all the Country hereabouts, especially on the Welsh side, greater expressions of joy then ordinary, & many Pulpits full of sharp Reflections upon the People concerned, only one I hear of whose Text was, Go teach all nations Baptising them - what he inferred from thence suitable to the occasion I know not. My love to your chamber-fellow unknown, help one another what you can especially for heaven, remembering wherein two are better then one. When you have leisure and can conveniently, go see your Aunts, but not by water, lest you catch cold, however write to them, if there bee such a way thither, by the Peny-post. What if you should call sometime at new Serj. Inn on Serj. Rigby or accost him, if you see him in Westmr hal, only to tel him who you are & what circumstances you are in, & to present my service to him & to inquire of the health & welfare of our fellow-Prisoners, as far as known to him. This is not to cut you out impertinent work, nor to engage you in inconveniences, but to intimate to you what you may doe, as there is occasion & if it fall in your way.
your Mother gives you her love and Blessing, your Father also his, The lord bee gracious to thee, my Son! Should you not pay respect some time to our land-lord?

Sr Roger Pu. went hence on Monday, his sister married to Mr. Thelw. Brine & Bron. are commended to you. Bee careful of your health, remember the rule venienti occurrere - but asp. neglegt not the mayn matter, the Soul is the man, if that doe well, ell's well.
Your letter escaped opening, write, but bee cautious what & how. - Nov. 13. 85.

I imagine, your present circumstances make it more difficult to your Friends to find you, else you would have more Visitants. It was a good Item written over a studious Person's study door Amiss, quisquis - Commend me to Mr. lower. what you appoint, as to your Debt to him, shall bee observed, but as to the other Affair, which himsf writes about, I can give no encouraging Answer, for several reasons, some of which, his own Consideration though not Affection, may suggest. Wee have hearty Sympathy with our Afflicted Friends in their Afflictions, weeping with those that weep, as being our selves also in the Body, Natural, Mystical. T'was a good Prayer of luther's when Melanct. & hee were entering the Place of Meeting at Spire, Domino Jesu, Tu ipse prospice Rebus tuis! In reading Bozo's Epist. I find, about 120. y. since, things were much at the same pass in the same climate, hee that hath delivered, doth deliver, & I trust, will. Amen! wee are thoughtful where & how you will spend this cold, dark, long vacation, without prejudice to ... your studies, your health; Our Prayer to God for you is that of Jabez for himsf daily, that the lord would bee with you & bless you indeed & enlarge your coast & keep you from the evil, from all evil, that it may not hurt you, even that the lord would preserve & keep your Soul! Amen & Amen! Dec. 11. .85.

note.value: 13. IN REPLY TO HIS SON'S OF DECEMBER 15TH.

text.p:
Yours came safe to hand & in due time this forenoon, finds us all in health, praised be God, & is as welcome to us, as or's can possibly be to you; They flock about it, as bees about a honey-comb, & are as much refreshed by it. I like not to have mine double-charg'd to you & to bee as dear as your dinner; had they been all in one sheet without slitting, I suppose, it had been otherwise. I am glad you have satisfied your curiosity in the sight of the Jewess worship, but more that you make such improvemt of it for the ends of true Piety; They are, certainly, to bee pitied by us, being under the sad influences of a dismal curse & judicial hardening, which yet there is hope will in due time, & therefore room for prayer, that it may, bee taken off when Popish Idolatry & Protestant Profanes, the great bars that hinder, shall come to an end, which God hasten for his mercy sake, & for their sake! Will you write a letter by the Post to Mr. Charles Williams
of Newpt in Monmouthshire to know of him, how it is with him & whether his Son bee bound Apprentice, if hee bee, to whom & for what, & where a legacy may bee paid in london for his use, giving a legal release; desire a line or two from him directed to you at Gr. Inn. Mr. W. Hr sent his Servant to me this week, for an old Acquittance I had of a Relief or herriot pt to ye E. of Derby 64. years since, which I sent him, whereby hee says I have much obliged him & I am very glad to doe it. Mr. Al. intends to stand suit with him, but I think, your counsel were better, to make peace; His Sister Mary is ill at present of the Small Pox, so are many more both in Town & Country, & or's yet spared, blessed bee the lord for it! his mercy to us therein is singular. Old Mrs. Bruerton, of Bella hill, Mr. Tho. Dod's Mother, died on Sabb. day last, her son is expected from London at her Intermt deferred till Tuesday next, as wee hear. Our usual yearly distribution is well performed & an account taken; that which puts the true value on it, is divine Acceptance, which is not wanting where there is uprightness; tic a good work, as Mr. Herbert said, when hee had built a church, if it bee sprinkled with the Blood of J. Xt without which all is nothing; See your need of him more & more & live upon him; no life like it, so sweet, so safe; christus mouse mihi in omnia ; Wee cannot be discharged from the Guilt of any evil wee doe, without his Merit to satisfy; wee cannot move in the performance of any Good required, without his S.p~it & grace to assist & enable for it, & when wee have done all, that all is nothing, without his Mediation & Intercession to make it Acceptable, so that every day in every th. hee is All in All.

Now the lord God everlasting bee your Sun & Shield in all your ways; see time hasting away apace towards eternity, & the Judge soon at the door, & work accordingly; wherever you are, alone or in company, bee always either doing or getting good, sowing or reaping. As for me, I make no other reckoning but that the time of my departure is at hand & what Trouble I may meet with before, I know not, the will of the lord bee done; One of my chief cares is, that no Iniquity of mine may bee laid up for you, which God grant for his mercy Sake in Christ Jesus. Amen!

The contents of your last doe a little trouble us, not so much that you were let Blood, though I think it might have been better had it been done sooner, as that you did mis-manage yourself after, both in going in the morning to lawrence Jury & in writing so much both to us & to Boreatton in the Evening, it being convenient after Blood-letting to bee sedate & composed for some time till Nature bee come to itself again; Therefore in your next I shall expect to hear, that you were worse after it, & that the Feebleness & Dullness you mention were the immediate Symptoms of it, which God in mercy prevent! Wee are all well here, thanks bee to God! The Divine Providence watching about our tabernacle, and compassing us about with Favour as with a Shield. our great Inquiry is, what shall we render! Alas, our rendrings are nothing to our receivings; wee are like the Barren field, on which much cost is bestowed, but the Crop is not accordingly; Our heavenly Father is Loding us with his Benefits & wee are Loding him with our sins, grieving him that comforts us, & how long, how long shall it be so! o`: that it might bee otherwise! that our Mercies might bee as Oil to the wheels, to make us so much the more active & lively in our Master's work, especi. considering how it is with our fellow-servants; They empty & wee full, they Marah, & wee Naomi. Our dear Friends Mr. Ja. Ow. at Oswestry & Mr. Jo. Wills. at Nantwich upon beds of sickness, & in the valley of the shadow of death, & wee well; They had hopes, when wee heard last, of the recovery of both of them though remaining dangerously ill. I am glad to hear your Aunts are in health, but sorry they are in any thing uneasy,
this is not the world, wherein wee must have everything that wee would have, but there is such a state before us, the happiness whereof eye hath not seen nor ear heard neither hath it entered into the heart of man to conceive; I would have you, as you have opportunity to bee a Comforter & a Counsellor to them, & as you can to help their Burdens. Tel Cos. Hobs. wee shall supply her son with such clothes as hee hath need of, & are fit for him, though she hath not mentioned it; you know your mother's way, she suffers nothing to spoil for want of mending in time. I saw Mrs. Tils. the other day, she heare's her son's Intentions for Holland are diverted for present, and yt hee will not bee at London till August; It seems, hee is unfixed, what should bee the reason? Her Sister Ben. seems to bee in a declining condition & I fear will not bee long in this world, but hath good hopes through grace of a better. Mr. Corbet had thoughts of sending his Horses back again, if so, it might doe some Friend a kindness that looks toward the Country, if you know of any such, & them no unkindness, to embrace the Opportunity, tho hee was not resolved. Hearty renewed respects to the worthy Trios of approved Friends mentioned in my last, whom I pray God to continue in their Integrity & Usefulness. There may a day come when it may cost dear to be honest, but after all, to fear god & keep his Commandmts is the whole duty of man. I therefore commend it to you, & you to God, who is a shield & Buckler to them that fear him.

Though wee have not yet received Cos. Hobsen's token, yet pray give her Thanks for it; Her son is well in health & learns his Catech. hee can say about half the first part & creeps on by degrees; wee should bee glad, if hee might get some good here, that might stick by him, Hee rode your Mare on Witnessed. (with your Sister Sarah on the little mare) to Ash & performed very well & last night hee rode to Whitch: & fetched your letter, which pleases him; Hee is glad to hear of his Mother & grandmother & hopes by this time they will have received his by Mr. Lawrence, who went hence, wee think on Monday. Mr. Corbet goes not till Tuesday next; Mr. Tong promises to cal on you; Tic now Vacation time, & though nulla dies sine Linea , yet Arcum non
semper tendit Apollo suum . It is not for me to sit here & prescribe neither when, nor how much, nor how long, but remember the counsel of my last, to bee always either doing, or getting good; you'll find his Company savoury, else I should not commend it to you, for I know you doe not want Company & I hope not good ones. Mr. Bentley was here yester-morning, told me hee saw you & sate a while with you; Tic Mercy wee may doe so in peace, si non data ultra` ; Mr. Birch came not to Will. last night, as expected, but at Preston hee said hee must bee, God willing, on Sabbath day.

wee read this morning in course, when wee had just newly experienced the Truth of it, by the receipt of your letter (for wee sent early to Whit. for it) Prove. 25. 25. As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so are good news from a far country. Since Friday last wee have been in aequilibrio , between hope & fear, not knowing what to think, that wee heard not from you; sometimes wee thought all was not well & then wee feared, expecting still by each Post some evil tidings, but when both Sat. & Monday. night brought noth. wee then began to conclude & hope it was, as it proves, but a miscarriage; But one, did I say? I am loath to determine where to fix it, neither can I, but as the Club-footed Philosopher whose shoes were stolen from him, only wished they might fit him that had them, so, not as hee intended but as the wish innocently seemed to mean at first hearing, I really innocently wish him that intercepted it this kindness, that the good sermons in it may doe his soul good, & that nothing else in it may doe you or us any hurt. It's being the first made it somewhat the worse. I am glad of the account you give of Westminr Election, being pleased with the story of it cold, though not as you were, who had it hot; Only one thing I miss, & that is the mention of my old Master, who used to bee the Principal verb, whether hee bee yet in vivis ; I don't remember that the second day was wont to bee like the first & thereof. your loss thereof was the less, asp.
having so good a sermon in exchange for it. It were not amiss if Ph. Bickl. would present hims. in propria persona to Sr Rogr Puleston at the Rolls for his Satisfaction for it is certainly believed here that hee is dead, & two Tenemts in which his life alone is, are, the one actually seized on & the profits detained for these two years past, the other which is John Griffiths of Addavellyn is threatened in like manner. John Griff. is so much concerned, that a Friend of his told me, hee would give Phil. a good peace of money could hee but see his Face. It is reported here, that Sr Job is for Chester again, is it so? Wee missed ye changes in ye Hal, besides all the rest. As to your Journey to Sussex, I know not what to say, bec. I know not how you are disposed; Is there a flying Coach thither? if so it may bee that were better than to hire a Horse; What company can you promise your sf? alone I would not have you, by no means, to venture in a strange country; The weather also is to bee considered, if it should continue dropping, the ways would bee bad there, either for Coach or Horse; so that after all, I must refer it to your sf; only Acknowledge God in all your ways & hee shall direct your steps; His Father talks sometimes of a Journey into Suffolk to lady Hr & so to Sussex all under one, but I see little likelihood of it. By this time, I suppose, Mr. An is with you from Oxon~. remember to bee like fire-stickes together, provoking one another to love & to good works, & to study at studying times, that your profiting may appear to all men. I am heartily sorry for the Death of the worthy Doctor, i.e. for the churche's loss in him, as for hims. hee is now no longer a stranger in a strange land; but at rest at home in his Father's house. Bee sure improve your Munday-evenings well & wisely, by sucking hard & pumping hard; you have not such Breasts every day & are to have those but a while, for our fashion passes away; If a wish would doe, I would be with you the very next, but it will not; Give my most Affectionate respects there however & to Mr. St. & Mr. l. & their yoke-fellowes. Your Father & Mother send you their Blessing, your sisters will some of them tel you thems. what they send you on the other side. Lord Delamere was at another Race last week at Fern, as I hear,
where hee won considerably of Squire Egerton; His Frds doe much wonder at the humour of it, & I think I told you formerly what the old woman said. What Fruit wee are like to have this summer upon the Trees, I cannot tel, they are yet but in Blossom, & Blossoms you know are not Fruit, but a sad Face of Barreness is upon our Congregations, many waxing worse & worse, few better better, And is the Axe laid to the Root? lord, let it alone this year also! Seeing your letters are so exposed, I need not renew the former caution to bee careful what you write; yet glad wee are to hear how it fares with the poor people of God in this gloomy day, who are our , that wee may rejoice with them when they rejoice & weep with them when they weep. As for any thing else, though wee are suspected to bee Men of Design, the Troublers. &c. our rejoicing is this, the Testimony - and let God alone in his way & time to clear the truth.

The weather hath been wet here of late, as it seems it hath been with you, but these two days last past have been fair & Summer-like & they that can are busy, though it bee late, sowing barley; were there the same care taken of the soul, in doing what wee can, when wee cannot doe what wee would, & to observe the Rule, better late than never, how well were it. Mr. Church went hence on Monday last, whom I suppose by this time you may have seen, hee took a letter for you & a Ginney, supposing you might have occasion. The chees-market is quite dead at present; something ails the londoners with Cheshire, thus to punish them. The Collection for ye French Protestants hath not reached us yet, but I suppose is coming; I saw the Narrative & could not choose but think, that things were made the worst of, for though I know what manner of spirit the people are of, yet
there were some passages, that would hardly consist with mere Humanity. I saw also the answer to the three Papers, & suppose by ye style its Author to bee Dr Sh. It confirms that which you have somet. heard a Friend of yours say, that there are some men, on whom if it should please Authority to Frown but half so much and half so long, as it hath done on some of their Neighbours, they would hardly hold their hand, so as they have done, however not their Tongues & Pens. Our God in all these events is bringing to pass his own will & counsel, which is for certain the advancemt of his own Kingdom & Glory, All which is prayed for in the three first Petitions of the lord's Prayer, to which all that love him will most heartily say, Amen! Though you have nothing of mine in ire hand now wherwithal to doe it, yet you must not forget to bring with you, if not to send before you on my account some small charity-Bookes (the quid asp.) for I am now quite out of stock, I gave 6d for one at Salop, whereas of Brom hims. I bought 6. for 7 groats. Also some small Bibles - I can buy them here for 2s 10d which is even cheap enough, but they are ill bound. I have not been in England this long time but purpose a sally shortly, God willing! Wee had a report of some disturbance in Coventry last Sabb. upon occasion of mass there, what truth is in it or what the circumstances were, wee hear not: Tic like Mr. Ch. may inform you, who was there a day or two after. You say no more of Prce, was the report of his Conformity true or false? Wee both send you our Blessing, your sisters & all ye rest their love & service. You have yet a Home here, & dear Relations together & not scattered nor broken up, how long it may bee so, God only knows, our times are in his hand, wee shall begin shortly to doe as the lads at Westmr were won't to doe, & it may bee do still, by the word Electio . Macte virtute, mi Fili, et vale! Dominus tecum!

we received ye tidings this morning of God's Goodness to you in ire Journey, for which wee desire to bee thankful; also a
further account of the late Fire & your loss therein & doe bless God it was no worse. If your Gown had been burnt, it might have been looked upon as a tacit super Sedaeas to your further Progress in those studies, but it is well it was not, however every Providence hath a voice & says something. Your kind entertainmt with Mr. A. at your first coming up must not divert you from your former methods, but get as soon as you can into the geares, volat irrevocabilis whore . As to the Chr business, I can say no more then I said both to them & to you together, when you were here, which was, that for the present you are under an engagemt another way; what may bee hereafter, God only knows; Tic not at all likely, that I should doe as you mention in the mean time, but if there bee a door of Opportunity I know none so fit to make use of it, as hee who is already with them upon the place, who knows them & is known of them. Ann walked afoot to Malpas to the burial of Widow Brinley & back again; when she was dying, she asked, was the money & ye Candle ready, the one whereof was put in the one hand & the other lighted in the other, at the time of her departure; they also sprinkled her & ye Bed & room with their holy water & fell a sweeping ye room with besoms, as hard as they could, to sweep all her sins away; o` that ever there should bee such darkness in the midst so much light! wee hear, the new lord Deputy was in some danger in his passage to Beaumaris, but escaped. The Whitchurch Curate took occasion on Monday last in his sermon to reflect upon the worth Mr. Baxter by name. One of our greatest Clergy-men lately being reproved for Associating hims. so much with Papists. answered, To inquire what Religion a man is of is as rude as to ask him, what money hee hath in his Pocket. remember us to Mr. Thomas Hunt, also tel him hee must bee busy, for now is his gathering time. Wee Both send you our dear love & Blessing, making mention of you in daily Prayer that you may bee serious & sincere, humble & fruitful! Amen! Feby. 4. 86/7.

Wee have at present a Calm here, all the noise is concer. many who are com'n lately out of Ireland; Two, who have brought their stock with them have bin bidding this week for Wellington Cross, whether a Bargain or no I know not. One Moor is expected to bee made Provost of ye College at Dublin, upon the lord Tyrconel's arrival. I thought Mr. Tylston would have deferred his Journey North-ward till nearer April, in regard the winter is not yet over; These two or three last days have been very cold here. I do not apprehend a Dr-ship likely to bee of any great advantage to him as yet, till hee hath years for it & more experience, but tic hard to get to bee mortified to a thing called worldly honour, though it bee indeed but a shadow. Wee all remember service to Mr. Thomas Hunt; tell him what Elizabeth Parsons said to Geor. Illidge about the Picture, turn away mine eyes from beholding vanity. The more dead hee is to the gay nothings of the Town, the more alive hee will bee to God & to his Duty. Mind him of what the Angel said to Elijah, what dost thou here Elijah? Wee are much beholden to Mr. Ast for his great kindness in so befriending you, but tic neither Portion nor relation, I would have you so much to look at in that matter, as the Person, that, as much as may bee, she be suitable & tried, wherein wee pray to God to direct you. There are more will have to say to you, as an Inns-of-Court Gentleman, then either as an N. C. M. or the son of one. Give my affectionate remembrance to the worthy Mr. Tal. & bee as oft with him, as you have opportunity, while you stay in Town; hee that walks with wise men shall bee wise. No tidings of late in any of your letters, as formerly, from Westmr Hal, I suppose, the reason to bee your not being in commons & thereof. not in a Gown; who succeeds chief J. Bedingf.? Tic reported here that Sr Tho. Jones doth, his Predecessor & his successor. Wee send you our Blessing, commending you to him, who Blesses indeed, in whose Favour life is. Amen!

I took all the two last to my Sf but now I shall have help for ye filling up of a half sheet. I rejoice in what you heard & felt & saw of God on Monday last, & hope it hath left upon you a truly indelible character & such impressions as no time nor any thing else shall be able to wear out. Remember, Assisted by thy strength, o` God I will - As to the manner & circumstances of your return, wee cannot order them here but must leave it to yoursf. to doe, as you shall see cause, beseeching the Lord in every th. to make your way plain before you, but as to the th. itsf. wee rejoice in hopes, it will not bee long now, ere wee shall see you here (tho multi cadunt inter -) and I must not say, bee filled with your company, for this is not the world that wee must bee together in; your Dear Mother hath no great joy in the thoughts of your closing with them at Chester upon the terms proposed, her reasons are weighty, & in other th. have many times swayed with me against my own, & it hath done well, what they are in this matter you shall hear immediately from hersf. As to your Northh affair wee are no little concerned about it, making mention of it, in every prayer, to our heavenly Father, who wee have learned, besides a common Providence hath a special hand in such disposals - Prove. 19. 14. And wee say, if you of all the other should miss it would - Gen. 26. 35 - Mr. Bentley had not his 20. till Thursday last, hee is now among the mountains but wee
expect him here to morrow; I attended Mr. Shn on Wed. last to his grave & heard Mr. Ma. there declare concer. him to this purpose, yt though hee had a favour for those of the separation yet the humour was wearing off & not long before his Death, hee expressed a Kindness for the Church of Engd as hee was informed, by whom & wherein, & how far, & why, I know not. - Should you not leave some small token of grateful remember. a Book or a Spoon or some th. in the hands of your worthy Frds that - The Clergy in Cheshire & Shropshire are hammering an Address of Thanks but divers of them will not strike - They begin to feel now for their oaths sake, & by our law he ought - Our love & Blessing is all here's room for and twice, within - without.
For Mr. Matthew Henry at Moldsworth about to bee ordained by the Presbytery, and - the following week to be married to Kath. d. of Samuel Hardware of Bromborough. Esquire. Jul. 1687.

I am very much concerned, that Two such great Affairs are at this time met together upon your hand, that of the next Sabb. & that of the week after; you know which of the two should fill you most, & I hope it will accordingly, & if it doe, you may the more comfortably expect a Blessing upon the other for ever. Since I knew anything in those matters, I have found it true that when I have been most careful in doing God's work, God hath been most faithful in doing mine. - I have not sealed but subscribed a Draught of Articles with Mr. Hardware, drawn after a fashion, but so, as may direct a better Pen, yet not without your help, & it is well you are so near to give it, for it seems to me so intricate as to some things, that a stranger who knows us not nor our circumstances may very easily mistake; Therefore see to it, as near as you can, that there bee none; Mr. Hr declares his meaning to bee that the 6 months bee mentioned, yet the Portion shall bee reckoned, as due from the day of Marriage, on which account, consideration is to bee had as to the Rent of the land. Wee were together yesterday at each place and upon view found every
thing, not worse, but rather better then represented. I have moved but cannot prevail, that seeing tic so much insisted on that competency should bee for the heir, that Probart's & Paynter's, should bee so allotted, besides which if ye 10lb p. ann. from Broad-Oke become payable there will bee a full hundred, as wee reckon it, for ye jointure. Peirs & Hughs & Henshaw - 50. Huxley & Robinson 40. & ye new field & chapfeilds which Huxley may use - 10 & ye 400: & with more you think fit of the 600 for younger children; But by all means let that bee plainly & clearly expressed, that it shall bee disposed of at such times & in such proportions to ye children, as you shall think fit, with our Advice; for Paternal Authority must bee preserved. As to time & Place of sealing, I would meet half way on Monday, but Witnessed. being the first day appointed at Hanmer, I must needs attend that. If you would not think it too long to defer till the week after, i.e. to ye 19th instant, I should hope by that time (your next Sabb. work & your Warrington journey & our engagemts here being all over) there would bee much more of clearness & freeness without hurry as to each circumstance, but I must not move it, however not insist on it, lest the heart bee made sick; therefore doe as you see cause, only in everything take God along with you & doe all in the name of the lord Jesus. Give my kind respect to your good Friend, whom I hope to cal by another name shortly. The lord Bless you Both, & first fit you for & then give you to each other in much Mercy! Amen!

note.value: 34. FOR MR. MATTHEW HENRY IN CHESTER.

text.p:
Wee were glad to hear by both your last, concerning yours & my Daughter's health in your new habitation, beseeching God to continue it to you, to your mutual comfort; wee also & or's here, are at present well, God bee praised! What you wrote concerning the Ordinaco~n at Warrington was welcome news, & wee rejoice in it, both that young ones are laying their hands at this time of day to the Gosp. plough & that the Gosp. way of their Admission to it is so publicly owned; I hear of two elsewhere that are in like circumstances & heartily pray the lord of the Harvest to thrust forth more & more, though there bee that thrust hard ag~t them. Shortly I expect Mr. Ashurst's son here, may wee not hope, you will give him & us a visit, when hee comes, being the younger & better horsed then I am at present. I go, God willing, in the morning to Women, to a Fast there, & whether thence to Boreatton, or to Hampton, where Dr Long is to bee on
Wednesday, I am not yet resolved - The ways are yet so exceeding bad for Women's travel that wee send not your sister Ann as you expect & she desires. I am troubld you have not more of the Books, my horse's weakness, & ye wayes' foulness agree not, & that's ye reason - you must digest those you have the better; asp. the Book of Books; Study that most & your own heart & the People's circumstances, & that will doe much.

note.value: 51. TO MR. MATTHEW HENRY AT CHESTER.

text.p: The Tidings of your growing illness, which met me at my return, abated much of the Comfort, which was wont, after a Journey, to make Home welcome, but blessed bee God, though Trouble & Fear lasted for the night, yet Joy came in the morning by my Son Hulton, who first told us of your being better; God in mercy perfect what hee hath begun, and sure you should bee careful of yourself, for Prayers ought to be seconded with endeavours; I doe not mean, you should spare yours. in the sense in which the Satan spake to Peter, for I see our Opportunities passing away, & I cannot say whatever others think, that you doe too much & should abate; but one thing, which I gave you a hint of, when with you, I again mind you of, & that is, in the loose you take, in your earnestness, keep the reins upon it & let it neither run too far, nor last too long, for I have mys. by experience found some prejudice by it, especially in my sight; And another thing, as to your Health, is, that being subject to Feavors as you are, I think you should not when you are warmed with preaching, either drink small Beer, which is an error on one hand, or Sack which is commonly offered, on the other, but both together, not a full draught but a little at a time, by degrees, & a little warmed not hot, which I find doth best, & I believe so will you; As to your daily diet, your Brother T. I perceive, hath advised you, but remember your sister S. & take heed of the extreme, which I believe she is still the worse for; She is your sister. Thence to Newp. on Monday, where the Net cast (& again at Weston on Tuesday) over many Fish, in hope; to God bee glory.

I doe willingly neglect no opportunity of writing to you, nor doe not you to me, though Paper bee growing dearer. Son Radf. (for whose safe return wee bless God) shows me the new Act of Indulgence, directed to you, concer. which I say, as wee used to say at School, when a whole play-day was expected & wee could have but an afternoon, est aliquid prodire tenus, si non datur ultra . There are several th. in it very acceptable, parts. freedom from Juries & Offices. &c. but it is a great way from hence' to Flint & how long wee may bee made to attend there, I know not; The quarrel is, will you let my people go, that they may serve me; wee will, but let them not go very far away, the men but not the women & children; the women & children but not the cattle, but let not Pharoh deal deceitfully any more; When God judges, hee will overcome. When you write to any of our law-makers, acknowl. their kindness & pains in procuring it with all thankfulness, but till the Sacramental Test bee taken off, our Business is not done. Tic off by sea, I hear, why not by land also? I published last Sabb. the Paper from Sr Pa. Ward. &c. concer. the Irish Collection, adding I could say no more to enforce it then is said there, for tic well penned, but our Parish-Officers either have not the Brief or are slow in reading it: for I doe not hear that any thing is done as yet, in pursuance of it. I should
add more but the Bearer's hast forbids - Our love & Blessing to you all, God fit us for parting Providence, by one for another! Amen!

I bless God, I have no evil tidings to send you concerning your Mother but rather good; She is, wee hope, creeping up the hill again & gathering by degrees a little strength & wee must not despise the day of the smallest things, it being greater & better then wee deserve. I did not think in the least to have widened our Family, but I know not how, it proves, wee doe. Sa. Wats. is come to us, besides Cos. Bens I asked her Father, whether if Mr. P. came, hee might have freedom with her, hee said, hee could not yet reconcile his mind to it, in regard of her Age; I said little to p~swade him now, having said enough formerly; that comes best that comes freely; nothing against the grayn; the world is wide. Wee heard of your sally to the Wood. &c. this
week & shall bee glad to hear a journal of it, especially that you are well after it, this sultry, sickly season. The Comrs have thought fit I should commence "Gent." though the Sessors returned me otherwise; The old spirit of enmity remains & works still, as far as there is Opportunity, & whilst they that hate us bear Rule over us, tic easy to tel what wee must look for, but blessed bee God the tedder is anything shortened! I hear, the Bil of Compreh. is on foot again, & much prosecuted by some, both Friends & Foes, the rather bec. it breaks the neck of the Sacramental Test. God, I hope, will turn all for good yet. Your Sistr Tilston is here yet, whether to stay till she is lighter, they are not yet resolved. Her Husbd is gone this even. to Boreatton. Farewell!

Wee had not heard, when I wrote last by James, of the Death of your good Friend Mr. Edwd Greg; I hope you are learning by it to cease from man, whose Breath is in his Nostrils, & to rest & stay your self on God only, who is the rock of Ages, & who alone lives for ever. Hee is both Jachin & Boaz too, our Creature-props are neither. Your Mother hath been afflicted this night with a Bee-sting yester-evening in her cheek, which not only made her face swell, but affected her all over, as you were once, not without but within also, for she was perfectly sick with it; I have not seen the like; how great a matter a little Fire kindles, wn armed with a Commission - I hear from Salop, not that the Minrs there, but many others, are dissatisfied with ye Articles; wee must never all bee of a mind, till wee come to Heaven; The 3. 8. & 16 have someth. in ym which without a candid construction would somewhat scruple me, so would the Bible its. strictly taken & in the letter, in those places which seem contradictory, were it not for such an Interpretation; yet I could wish it had not been required, bec. it divides us.

Can you not send me word by Mr. Booth or Mr. Parry's
information, when our Sessions are? I hear yours is past & all done. I go tomorrow, God willing, to Oswestry.

note.value: FOR MRS. KATHERIN HENRY AT CHESTER.

text.p:
Every day a letter would bee a Book in time. I wrote yesterday by Son Tylst. which I hope you received; I forgot to tel you the malt is ready for my Son, but no Barley bought yet for ours. the reason is the dearness; 8 groats ye least in Whitch. did not I hear Mr. Bolland say, hee had in Chester for 2. 3d? if so might not the same Horses bring us 20 of Barley from thence, that brings ye 20 of Malt from hence, if so & you please, get it bought on Sat. Two swine John bought at Whitch. & Hempseed, to day hee begins to sow Barley; I am more & more for son Tylst. pulling the old house down, rather in repairing it, a new one will bee cheaper then hee thinks & I am sure much more inviting to a Tenant, asp. for warmth upon that wet & cold bank, 'twil need no repairing, a little will fit what will bee needful while it is as it is; the rest by degrees at leisure. 50. thous. of brick 10lb, 4 cart-load of lime, the workman tells me to day will lay ym which is 20s, besides ye carriage, & 10lb the workmanship, which will bee the walls. The old Timber will most of it serve (the rest may bee sold) joists, doors, Boards, ye carpenters' work about it cannot bee, for present 15lb & the Covering not 15. more, which is all, besides glazing what is to bee used, the rest brick't up. A trusty man, such as Randle Catheral, to oversee both pulling down and rearing would bee had for a little, summering there or thereabouts. The building 10. yards square, & 8. yds high, for 3 stories besides ye Cellar, would bee a mean; You know, who said, I only propose. yester-morning in the same hour 5. clock, wn Mr. Bradley departed, a grand-son was born to his Daughter Matthews. I am told they are to have one of the hundreds. The church-warden at Whitch. sent for leave to bury him to morrow in the burying place of ye Family, which I, supposing my son will not deny, granted. John K ... went yesterday to
Oxford with a Troup of Whitch. Minims, but would have my leave first. My bones are not yet eased of yesterd. riding, else God bee praised, well. love & blessing to all & each, again & again & again.

Sarah Green's little one is ill. Sisters love to you & to all ye rest. I hope, John may bee with you by 9. or 10. clock, which will bee as soon as you will bee ready. Mr. Wright comes in stead of Sam. Wait; Farewell, The God of love & peace bee with you. Amen!
